aiopslab.interpretation: these are executable contracts in AIOpsLab and are retained as an external capability comparison; this project's loopback fault injection, action and recovery readback are measured in the separate live-site snapshot

measured.definition: firing alert yields at least one asset, bounded time, fault domain, and overlap with the labelled affected alert group

business_values.remaining_gap: seven ITBench scenarios still lack complete public alert scope; the live-site takeover result is reported independently
public tests rank candidates; they do not show a new model-origin hypothesis being probed and confirmed; the live-site row measures that separate step
public held-out cases measure telemetry-grounded publication; live model-origin roots are measured separately by session receipts
candidate rank remains an offline search-cost proxy; the live-site row uses same-incident repeated wall-clock and probe-count comparisons
AIOpsLab recovery functions remain external capability evidence; this project's isolated execution, stability readback and failed recovery are measured live
the public replay measures no-negative-transfer ordering, while the live-site row measures repeated incidents with the same root and fewer real probes

claim_boundary: public replay measures parsers, candidate retrieval, deterministic localization, grounded publication and paired memory ordering. The live-site snapshot is a separate controlled fault-injection cohort; neither evidence level substitutes for the other

automatic_scope.definition: firing alert yields at least one asset, bounded time, fault domain, and overlap with the labelled affected alert group

event_retrieval.missing_evidence_policy: a scenario with no root-bearing Kubernetes event is excluded from retrieval accuracy and remains unresolved for this evidence source
